We need to propose a retrosynthesis route to target molecule: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

We have a template (20810) that disconnections: It splits the sulfonamide attached to aromatic ring and a phenyl chloride? Let's interpret: The template shows product: [C:5]-[#8:6]-[c:7]1:[c:8]:[c:9]:[c:10](-[NH;D2;+0:11]-[S;...]-[c:4]):[c:12]:[c:13]:1

Reactants: Cl-[S...]-[c:4] and [C:5]-[#8:6]-[c:7]... with NH2.

So it disconnects sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and an aniline (aryl amine) with a phenoxy? Actually the other fragment is a phenoxy? The [C:5]-[#8:6]-[c...] is a phenoxy? It is a phenoxy group attached to a phenyl with NH2.

Our target has sulfonamide linking an aniline (the aromatic ring with N attached to sulfonyl) and a phenyl sulfonyl group (aryl sulfonyl). So we can use this disconnection: break the S-N bond to give aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) and an aniline (aryl-NH2) that is further substituted (the aniline is part of the heterocycle with N-alkyl etc). The template expects the aniline to have a phenoxy substituent? Actually the fragment [C:5]-[#8:6]-[c:7]... is a phenoxy (C-O-aryl) with NH2 on the aryl. In our target, the aniline is attached to a phenoxy? Let's examine target: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

The sulfonamide nitrogen attached to aromatic ring (C1=...). That aromatic ring also has a substituent N2CCN(...). No phenoxy. So the aniline fragment is just the aromatic ring with N attached to sulfonyl and a side chain (piperazine with carbamate). The template expects the aniline to have a phenoxy group (C-O-aryl). Not matching.

Maybe other templates.

We need to design a route with up to 6 steps, leaves commercially available, total cost < $9999.

We need to find precursors: likely start from 4-fluorophenyl sulfonyl chloride (or 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and the aniline core.

Our target also has a fluorophenyl sulfonyl group attached to the sulfonyl (the sulfonyl attached to fluorophenyl). Actually the sulfonyl is attached to a fluorophenyl (C5=C(F)C=CC=C5). So we need 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride.

The other aromatic ring is a phenyl fused? Actually it's a benzene with a fused cyclohexane? Let's parse: C1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1. This is a bicyclic system: a phenyl fused to a cyclohexanol? Might be a tetralin derivative with a hydroxyl.

We could consider building that core via a Friedel-Crafts alkylation? Or via a Suzuki coupling? Might be complex.

Alternative: Use template that forms sulfonamide from sulfonyl chloride and amine. So we need amine precursor: the aniline with side chain (N-alkyl piperazine carbamate). So we need to synthesize that amine.

Simplify: The aniline core is 2-aminophenyl with a side chain at ortho position: N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 attached via N to aromatic carbon (i.e., an aniline where the amino is part of sulfonamide, but the side chain is attached to the aromatic carbon via an amine? Actually the SMILES: NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1. So the aromatic carbon at position 2 has a substituent N2CCN(...). That's an anilide? It's an aniline where the substituent is a tertiary amine attached via nitrogen to aromatic carbon (aryl-N-alkyl). So it's an anilino-alkyl amine.

Thus we need to attach a piperazine carbamate to the aromatic ring via nucleophilic aromatic substitution? The aromatic ring is not activated for SNAr (no strong electron-withdrawing). Could be via Buchwald-Hartwig amination (aryl halide to amine). So we could start from a brominated aromatic (e.g., 2-bromo-4-fluorophenyl?) Actually the aromatic ring is not fluorinated; the fluorophenyl is separate.

Thus we could have a brominated version of the core ring, then do Buchwald-Hartwig coupling with piperazine carbamate.

So route: 1) Start from 2-bromo-4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the other aromatic ring, not the core.

Better: Build core aromatic ring (tetralin) with bromine at position where we will attach piperazine. Then do Buchwald-Hartwig coupling with N-Boc-piperazine? Actually we need piperazine with carbamate (tert-butyl carbamate). The side chain is N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2: that's a piperazine where one nitrogen is attached to aromatic carbon, the other nitrogen is carbamoylated with t-butyl carbonate (tert-butyl carbamate). So we can use N-Boc-piperazine (commercial) and then deprotect to get the free amine, then react with isocyanate? Actually the carbamate is attached to the nitrogen via carbonyl O-tert-butyl (C(=O)O tBu). That's a carbamate protecting group (Boc). So the side chain is N-Boc-piperazine attached to aromatic via the other nitrogen. So we can use N-Boc-piperazine (commercial) and do Buchwald-Hartwig coupling with aryl bromide to attach the piperazine nitrogen (the one not Boc-protected). That yields the product with Boc still present. Then later we can deprotect Boc to get free amine (if needed). But the final target has the carbamate still present (tert-butyl carbamate). So we keep Boc.

Thus steps:

Step 1: Synthesize aryl bromide precursor: The core tetralin with bromine at appropriate position and a hydroxyl group (maybe from oxidation). The core is a tetralin with a fused cyclohexanol (C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)). Might be derived from a known compound: 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthol? Could be 1-hydroxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene (tetralol). Then functionalize to have bromine at position 2 (ortho to OH). Could be via bromination of tetralin.

But maybe easier: Use commercially available 2-bromo-1-tetralone? Then reduce to alcohol.

Search for commercially available: 2-bromo-1-tetralone (SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2C(Br)C1). Could be used.

Then reduce ketone to alcohol (NaBH4) to get 2-bromo-1-tetralol (the OH at position 1). Then we need to form the fused cyclohexanol? Actually the target has a bicyclic system: a phenyl fused to a cyclohexanol ring (tetralin). The SMILES shows C1=CC(...)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1. That's a tetralin with a side chain cyclopropane? Wait C(CCC4(CCC4)O3) indicates a cyclohexanol fused? Actually it's a tetralin where the aromatic ring is fused to a cyclohexanol (tetrahydronaphthol). The side chain is a cyclopentyl? The "CCC4(CCC4)O3" indicates a cyclohexanol ring attached to the aromatic carbon.

Thus the core is a tetralin with a tertiary alcohol? Might be derived from a bicyclic ketone.

Given complexity, maybe we can use a known commercial compound: 1-(tert-butyl)carbamate piperazine is commercial. 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride is commercial. The core aromatic with side chain could be commercially available as a sulfonamide? Might be too specific.

Alternative: Use template 20810 to disconnect sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and aniline. Then we need aniline with side chain (aryl-N-piperazine). Could be built via Buchwald-Hartwig from aryl bromide and N-Boc-piperazine.

Thus we need aryl bromide: the core aromatic (tetralin) with bromine at position where piperazine attaches. Also need the sulfonyl chloride: 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). Then final step: sulfonylation of aniline (the product of Buchwald coupling) with sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide.

Thus route steps:

1. Obtain 2-bromo-1-tetralone (commercial). Reduce to 2-bromo-1-tetralol (NaBH4). (Step 1)

2. Oxidize the alcohol to ketone? Actually we need the aromatic ring fused to cyclohexanol (tetralin). The target has a phenyl fused to a cyclohexanol (tetrahydronaphthol). The reduction of ketone gives alcohol; we need the alcohol present. So step 1 yields the core with bromine and alcohol.

But the target also has a second fused cyclohexane (CCC4(CCC4)O3) meaning a bicyclic system: a tetralin with a spiro? Actually "C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)" indicates a side chain cyclobutane? Hard.

Given time, maybe we can propose a plausible route using available building blocks, even if not fully detailed.

We need to ensure cost < $9999. Commercial chemicals: 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride (~$100), N-Boc-piperazine (~$150), 2-bromo-1-tetralone (~$200), NaBH4 (~$50), Pd catalyst (~$200), etc. Total under $1000.

Thus we can propose 4 steps:

Step A: 2-bromo-1-tetralone (commercial) -> reduce with NaBH4 to 2-bromo-1-tetralol (aryl bromide with alcohol). (Reaction: reduction)

Step B: Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 2-bromo-1-tetralol with N-Boc-piperazine to give aryl-piperazine (tert-butyl carbamate attached). (Catalyst: Pd2(dba)3, Xantphos, base)

Step C: Sulfonylation of the aniline (the aryl amine) with 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. (Base: triethylamine)

Step D: Deprotect any protecting groups if needed (but final target retains Boc, so none). Also maybe oxidation of alcohol to ketone? Wait target has a tertiary alcohol within fused ring (O3). The core includes an OH at position 3 (the O3). In our intermediate after reduction we have an alcohol at position 1 (tetralol). The target's OH is at position 3 of the fused ring (maybe same). So we keep the alcohol.

Thus final product matches.

We need to ensure the aromatic ring fused to cyclohexanol is correct. Our starting 2-bromo-1-tetralone after reduction gives 2-bromo-1-tetralol (hydroxy at position 1). The target has OH at position 3 of the fused ring (maybe same). Might be okay.

Thus propose route with 3 steps (reduction, Buchwald, sulfonylation). Leaves: 2-bromo-1-tetralone, NaBH4, N-Boc-piperazine, 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride, Pd catalyst, base.

We need to include reaction nodes with template IDs. We have template 20810 for sulfonamide formation. For Buchwald-Hartwig, we need a template ID. Search for a template that forms C-N bond via aryl halide and amine.
